title: `self::m()` and `parent::m()` inside a closure call the class the closure is written in
scope:
the called class of a `self::m()` or `parent::m()` call, or `(...)` reference, written inside a
closure body. `static::` in a closure stays refused ([0211](0211.md)'s `E0834`), and the same calls in
a method body still forward the method's called class.
dependsOnText:
[0008](0008.md) (`static` marks a class member and keeps its PHP meanings),
[0144](0144.md) (`static::class` is a run-time read of the called class a frame holds),
[0211](0211.md) (`static::` in a closure is refused).

summary.headline: `self::` in a closure calls the class the closure is written in
summary.body:
A closure in a method can call `self::m()` and `parent::m()`. If `m` is a static method,
`static` inside it is the class the closure is written in. PHP uses the class the outer method was
called on. An instance method called this way uses the closure's `$this`.
